set.st: In March 1902 workmen grading a Muscatine lot just sold to a Mr. Koehler, long the homestead of the widow Mrs. C. Kegel and her daughter, dug up a rusted tin can of $20, $10 and $5 gold pieces and about $200 in silver dimes. Four men scrambled for the coins: the first got about $130, the rest from $45 down to ten cents. No remainder was reported. The same item recalls that 'several years ago' on West Seventh Street, after a reclusive widow landlord died, the new owners grading the lot found a pot with over $1,600 in gold, also recovered. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.v: A can of gold pieces and about $200 in dimes (1902); an earlier $1,600 pot on West Seventh St (1890s)
set.t: Both Muscatine finds were recovered on the spot. City lots, built over: look-only.
set.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): recovered 1902; nothing reported left
src: Evening Times-Republican (Marshalltown), 27 Mar 1902, p. 3, 'Find Pot of Gold' (LoC Chronicling America; Newspapers.com 352056509)

set.pl: Fay ravine, Lake Prairie Twp, Nicollet Co, between Le Sueur and St Peter: the creek ravine where it crosses Bernard Fay's 80, W edge sec. 8 T111N R26W (1899 atlas)
pinev: Barney Fay ravine: Bernard Fay 80, W edge sec 8 T111N R26W, Lake Prairie Twp (1899 atlas; 1900 census); creek crosses the tract.
On 2023 MN 1 m lidar the ravine crosses the Fay strip between about 44.432 and 44.436 N, floor near 264 m against 291 m uplands; pin on the creek floor there, ring covers that reach and both banks.
set.t: The 1890 account found a hideout, not a cache; any loot is inference. Private farmland: ask permission.

tw-mn-fay-ravine-dugout-1890.st: The St Paul Globe (Le Sueur, 19 Dec 1890) says the rabbit hunters were going up 'what is known as the Barney Fay ravine from its foot … toward its head' when they found a strapped door in the creek bank. Behind it were a dug-out anteroom, the 20 x 16 ft bunk room and a cave stable for 20 horses. Inside were a letter headed 'Elysian, Minn., April 8 … Friend Jim … Frank', read as James-Younger or horse-thief talk ('Half-Way'), a vest with 75 cents in old paper money and a 'J. S. Rivers' envelope, and the skull under cornstalks.
src: St Paul Daily Globe, 20 Dec 1890, p. 2
Atlas of Nicollet County (1899), Lake Prairie plate; US census 1900, Lake Prairie (Bernard Fay, b. 1828 Ireland)
